title: Adaptive Model Signal Canvas — Continuous competitive observability and engineering handoff
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a repeatable canvas and lightweight instrumentation to continuously detect differentiating model feature signals (latency regressions, token-cost regressions, new API capabilities, hallucination pattern changes) and route them into an operations-ready handoff for engineering, research, and GTM. This ticket scopes the PM side: target metrics, alert thresholds, consumers, dashboards, and the canonical handoff template that engineers use to triage and onboard model-specific mitigations.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical 'Adaptive Model Signal Canvas' document exists in Confluence and is approved by PM + Eng leads
Three signal types (latency, cost-per-token, quality-drift) have defined thresholds and automated guards mapped to owners
A Grafana dashboard prototype aggregates model-level indicators and links to the canvas from the alert panel
An engineering handoff template (minimal reproducible repro + perf traces + failing prompts) is in the repo and validated by one trial handoff
On-call and SRE routing flow is documented and validated with a tabletop exercise
updates: 2025-02-18 Aisha Patel — Kickoff: aligned scope with Eng Lead (Luca), Research (Maya), and Observability (Jon). Agreed to prioritize three signal classes for MVP (latency, token-cost, embeddings drift).
2025-02-22 Luca Moreno — Drafted canvas fields: signal source, sampling cadence, owner, impact bucket, quick triage steps, fallback policy. Shared with ENG and Research for feedback.

2025-02-25 Maya Chen (Research) — Feedback: for quality-drift include prompt-set anchored evaluations + baseline generation hash to reduce noisy alerts. Suggested automated snapshotting of eval prompts.

2025-02-27 Jon Rivera (Observability) — Proof-of-concept Grafana panel up at https://grafana.redwood.example/d/model-signals (internal). Panel uses Metrics API: model.latency.p50, model.tokens.avg_cost, embeddings.cosine-drift. Needs standardized tags (model, region, deployment-type).

2025-03-01 Aisha Patel — Decision: MVP will surface contextual links (PRD, GH PR, failing prompt set) inside alerts. Trade-off: narrower scope faster to delivery vs. catching fewer edge-case signals. Chosen faster delivery.

2025-03-03 Luca Moreno — Engineering handoff template added to repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-signals/tree/main/handoff-template. Includes checklist, repro script, KV cache dump sample, and perf trace instructions. Running trial handoff with ENG-4120.
2025-03-04 Aisha Patel — Updated acceptance criteria and scheduled tabletop exercise for 2025-03-12 with SRE + On-call + PMs. Next: finalize Confluence canvas and map to alerting rules.
links: Example GH issue created by trial handoff: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/4120
notes_for_engineering: Provide a lightweight endpoint that exports standard tags (model_id, model_variant, region, deployment_type) for all metrics so the Grafana panel can be model-agnostic.
Include a small sampled prompt-set snapshot in the handoff bundle (max 50 prompts) with anonymization rules documented.
Export KV-cache meta and a pointer to tokenization artifacts; avoid including raw customer PII in snapshots.
Instrument per-model token-cost as a first-class metric (tokens.consumed * unit_cost) to detect sudden cost regressions after quantization or model swaps.
Ensure alert suppression windows configurable per-project to avoid noisy false positives during rollouts.

Complete Grafana panel instrumentation and standard tags by ENG-1842
Run 1st tabletop on 2025-03-12 and document learnings
